reveal.summary: The Outsiders. A missile, a marshal, a Beatles street, a stranded millionaire and a soft drink — every answer is a cast list in disguise: Tom Cruise, Matt Dillon, Diane Lane, C. Thomas Howell, and Sodapop Curtis. Francis Ford Coppola's 1983 adaptation was a nursery for future stars — and its four words came from a Robert Frost poem: nothing gold can stay.
reveal.ohMoment: The subjects were feints — History's missile and TV's marshal were actors all along. And if you typed 'stay golden': that's the famous misquote. The line was always 'Stay gold.'

editorial.notes: Showcase of the double-meaning mechanic: every answer is a common word that is ALSO a cast name (Cruise, Dillon, Lane, Howell) plus one inside-story anchor (Soda). Canonical-phrase rule: 'Stay gold, Ponyboy' — 'stay golden' is the widespread misquote, used as a reveal factoid. Letter curve: S(1) → T(1) → A(1) → Y(3) → O(3); full success reveals 9 of 15 letters (60%).
